catalog_quote: Stress or phonological prominence in Enxet Sur cannot be adequately summed up by a generalization like “stress is typically on the penultimate syllable”. Discussions of stress in previous descriptions of ES or related languages has been overly simplistic, and has surely relied on the phonological intuitions of linguists whose native languages were western European. ... Identifying a discrete “stress” unit is not particularly obvious, and the acoustic correlates of stress/prominence appear to interact with both syllable weight (presence/absence of codas or long vowels) and the morphological structure of words, since roots and bases must maintain some prominence while some other affixes cannot be “stressed”. ... Just from these simple examples, it is clear that interactions between intensity and pitch are complex, and need to be defined more clearly before we can assert which syllable has…

audit.reasoning: The classification 'undetermined' rests on the only comprehensive description of Enxet Sur, a 794-page 2021 reference grammar that we hold in full, and the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated section and pages. The author explicitly refuses a stress-position generalization, backs that with Praat pitch/intensity figures showing weight- and morphology-dependent prominence, and dismisses the only prior claim (Powys 1929 penult) as limited; our prule/srule/heavy fields reflect this accurately. No later phonology, JIPA illustration, or instrumental prosody study of Enxet Sur turned up in Crossref/Cambridge Core/Wikipedia/IA checks (Elliott 2016 JASA is vowels; Elliott et al. 2025 IJAL is grammaticalization).
